L01.text: In nineteen thirty-two, Australia sent soldiers with machine guns to fight a war against emus. The emus won.

L02.text: Western Australia. A drought sends about twenty thousand emus into the wheat fields, flattening crops and fences.

L03.text: The farmers ask for help. The army sends Major Meredith, two machine guns, and ten thousand rounds.

L04.text: First ambush: the emus walk right up to the dam. The gun fires a few shots, and jams.

L05.text: So they bolt a gun onto a truck. But emus sprint at about fifty kilometers an hour, over ground the truck can't handle.

L06.text: By the army's own count, they fired nine thousand eight hundred and sixty rounds, for nine hundred and eighty-six birds.

L07.text: That's about ten bullets per emu.

L08.text: Luckily, the army brought ten thousand bullets. Unluckily, the emus brought twenty thousand emus.

L09.text: The army went home. The farmers went back to bounties. And the emus never signed a peace treaty.
